corrected_verdict: KNOWN, in technique as well as result. Step 1 (|det(I+tH)| <= prod(1+t|d_l|), and the coefficientwise e_k(x) >= C(nu,k)) is the Seiler-Simon 1975 determinant inequality (Thms 1, 1'', 2'), iterated over the rank-one summands. Step 2 (integrate the log of a generating-function comparison to reach power sums) is Weyl's own 1949 proof device (kernel log max(1,lambda z), eqs. 8-10); the paper's kernel log(1+xt) is the Thorin-Bernstein kernel, and Remark 'other penalties' describes exactly the Thorin-Bernstein functions. The inequality also follows from Weyl majorant + Rotfel'd-Thompson, as the checker said. What the paper actually works out is the equality characterization: nu equal-modulus terms with orthonormal chain vectors, i.e. rows of a dephased complex Hadamard matrix. The checker's verdict stands, but its Horn-Johnson bib entry carries the wrong DOI.
issues: (1) The confirmed citation hornjohnson2012 has a wrong DOI. 10.1017/CBO9780511810817 is the 1985 1st edition: the cambridge.org page the checker cited shows print year 1985, and Crossref lists edition 1. The 2nd edition (2012) is 10.1017/CBO9781139020411 (Crossref edition 2, 2012-10-22). Also, 'Sylvester's identity' in Horn-Johnson usually names the bordered-minor identity, so the paper should write det(I+AB)=det(I+BA) explicitly; section numbers are unverified. (2) bhatia1997: metadata confirmed via Crossref, but the checker's confirming URL was Amazon, and the locators Thm II.3.6 and Ch. V are unverified. Do not print them unchecked. (3) Missed prior art for the technique itself: Seiler & Simon, PNAS 72(9):3277-3278 (1975), is exactly Step 1 and uses the same coefficient-domination proof. Weyl 1949 pp. 409-411 is exactly Step 2 (generating-function comparison g(z) <= f(z), then phi = int log max(1,lambda z) d psi). Weyl also remarks that prod(1+lambda_i^s z) is majorized coefficientwise. (4) The 'generating-function-to-power-sum transfer' that the checker said had no named precedent has one: Weyl's device, plus the Thorin-Bernstein class (Schilling-Song-Vondracek 2012, Ch. 8, 'Thorin-Bernstein functions', pp. 109-116 per Crossref; chapter text not fetched). (5) thompson1976 and weyl1949 are confirmed from primary sources (Thompson PDF text; Weyl page images). The Bernstein constant r sin(pi r)/pi was checked numerically.

extra_citations.why: Thm 1'' gives |det(1+A+B)| <= det(1+|A|)det(1+|B|), and Thm 2' is the coefficientwise version |d_m(A+B)| <= sum_k d_k(|A|)d_{m-k}(|B|). Iterated over the rank-one summands t d_l u_l u_l^*, these are exactly Step 1 of app:cost: eq. (cost-generating) and e_k(x) >= C(nu,k). Their proof also compares polynomial coefficients. Cite at Step 1.

Corrected entry: the 2nd-edition DOI, verified on cambridge.org and Crossref. Use it for det(I+AB)=det(I+BA), the principal-minor expansion, and Hadamard's inequality. The checker's DOI points to the 1985 1st edition.

Ch. 8, 'Thorin-Bernstein functions' (pp. 109-116, per Crossref chapter records), is the class a + bx + int log(1+x/t) sigma(dt). That is exactly the class in Remark 'other penalties' and the kernel of Lemma bernstein. Metadata and chapter title are verified; the theorem number inside the chapter is not. Series and volume (De Gruyter Studies in Mathematics 37) are not verified, so they are omitted.

Optional. The equality case of Lemma cost (nu pairwise-orthogonal unimodular chain vectors in C^nu) says the m_l are the rows of a dephased complex Hadamard matrix; the nu-block is the Fourier matrix. One clause in Remark 'orthogonality as roots of unity' would name the object.
